title: Async Methods in Trait Objects
goal: Understand why async fn in traits requires Boxed futures for trait objects.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Async Traits

sections.text: Rust allows `async fn` inside traits. However, because each `async fn` returns a unique, un-namable future type, traits with `async fn` cannot be made into trait objects (`dyn Trait`).

sections.caption: An async fn in a trait returns an implicit opaque type.

sections.text: To use an async trait with dynamic dispatch (`dyn Trait`), the return type must be an explicit boxed pinned future: `Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = T>>>`.

sections.caption: Pin<Box<dyn Future>> provides a uniform type for dynamic dispatch.

sections.text: The `async_trait` crate automates this transformation using a procedural macro. Knowing the underlying pinned box explains what that macro generates under the hood.

explanation: Understand why async fn in traits requires Boxed futures for trait objects.
